snapshots.title: Eli’s return trip
snapshots.alt: Eli walks 6 m east from the starting marker, then 6 m west back to it.
snapshots.body: Follow both arrows. Then compare the starting and finishing markers.
snapshots.question: How can the same trip have 12 m of distance and zero displacement?
snapshots.work: Part 1 · Compare the path and endpoints

snapshots.title: The courtyard route
snapshots.alt: A notebook shows five equal steps north, three east, and five south. The whole route is 13 step-lengths; its displacement is 3 step-lengths east.
snapshots.body: The dashed route follows every leg. The direct arrow joins the start to the finish.
snapshots.question: What must be true about the steps for the north and south changes to cancel?

snapshots.title: A number needs a direction
snapshots.alt: Two alternative one-million-kilometer displacements start at the same asteroid position. One points toward Earth and one points away. These are possibilities, not a forecast.
snapshots.body: The two arrows have the same magnitude and different endpoints. Neither is a forecast.
snapshots.question: What information and observations would distinguish these possibilities?
snapshots.work: Part 3 · Give the headline a direction
